notes.gloss: exaggeratedly proper
notes.note: Too proper to the point of being easily shocked, and so a harsher word than *prim*.

notes.gloss: not suitable or right or appropriate
notes.note: The flattest disapproval here - it marks a thing as not fitting without naming the standard it fails, where *unseemly* and *indecent* name one.

notes.gloss: yielding material gain or profit
notes.note: The flat starting point: it reports a gain but not its size or how welcome it is - the two things *juicy* adds.

notes.gloss: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
notes.note: The weightiest plain word for a wanted outcome: it gives the planned action its reason, where *aim* only gives it a direction.

notes.gloss: designed to promote discipline
notes.note: Official, and a gentler way to name discipline - it is what discipline is called in a report.

notes.gloss: aroused to impatience or anger
notes.note: Rude and blunt: the crudest way in this group to say it, and everything *displeased* holds back.

notes.gloss: out of working order (‘busted’ is an informal substitute for ‘broken’)
notes.note: Only says the thing does not work - not how it got that way, which is nearly all *battered* tells you.

notes.gloss: smelling of cinnamon
notes.note: Warm where *mint-scented* is cool, but the warmth belongs to the spice, not the word, which names the smell flatly.

notes.gloss: developed or executed with care and in minute detail
notes.note: The *-ed* form, cooler than *elaborate*: it marks a thing as having been worked out rather than admiring the result.

notes.gloss: precisely and clearly expressed or readily observable; leaving nothing to implication
notes.note: The neutral base word here: so clear that nothing is left to work out, without praising or criticising that clarity.

notes.gloss: manifesting partiality
notes.note: Accusing where its neighbours approve - it treats favouring one side as the wrong itself, not as a favour worth having.

notes.gloss: tell anonymously
notes.note: The point is the missing name: the teller stays out of sight, and the word passes no judgement on what is told.

notes.gloss: a deliberate pretense or exaggerated display
notes.note: A charge of deliberate faking or of overdoing it, so the fault is excess as much as falseness.

notes.gloss: far beyond a norm in quantity or amount or degree; to an utmost degree
notes.note: Names the utmost degree flatly, measuring how far an amount or degree sits from the norm without calling that a fault.

notes.gloss: painful as if caused by a sharp instrument
notes.note: The *-ing* twin of *lancinate*, just as clinical, but the pain is still going on as it is described.

notes.gloss: (of sound or color) free from anything that dulls or dims
notes.note: With its *un-*, it praises a sound or colour by naming what fails to cloud it, where *clear* simply states the brightness.

notes.gloss: an old woman
notes.note: A pet name for any old woman, grandmother or not - familiar where *mother* is respectful, and it shrinks her to her age.

notes.gloss: strongly marked; easily noticeable
notes.note: Raises the degree, not the ease: the thing stands out by how strongly it shows, not by how easily it is found.

notes.gloss: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
notes.note: Strips the cover off, suggesting the thing was kept back for a reason, so telling it accuses whoever kept it.

notes.gloss: having or showing or requiring special skill
notes.note: Plain, checkable praise that credits skill without admiring it, and can describe work that needs skill as well as people who have it.

notes.gloss: poorly done
notes.note: The flat word here: it says only that the work fell short of skill, with none of the disgust in *butcherly*.

notes.gloss: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
notes.note: Flat and unemotional - it states the thing takes effort to do, grasp or bear, without *challenging*'s hint that the effort is worth it.

notes.gloss: giving an advantage
notes.note: Cool, calculating approval: it weighs only the edge a thing gives you, not whether that edge is deserved or does any good.

notes.gloss: beyond belief or understanding
notes.note: Puts the thing wholly past belief or understanding, not just very unlikely, and says nothing of whether that is wonderful or awful.

notes.gloss: kill intentionally and with premeditation
notes.note: The most indirect way here to say it: a planned killing made to sound like tidying, its intent hidden behind a bland word.

notes.gloss: a person who founds or establishes some institution
notes.note: Deeply respectful: it makes the founder the institution's parent, giving it a family line and the founder a right to thanks.

notes.gloss: lacking the requisite qualities or resources to meet a task
notes.note: Weighs what is brought against what the task needs and finds a mismatch, where *inadequate* calls the lack a fault in the thing.

notes.gloss: accompanied by bloodshed
notes.note: Puts a butcher's hand on the bloodshed - crude, like a day's work, and scornful of whoever did it, where *slaughterous* is merely grand.

notes.gloss: spoiled or ruined or demolished
notes.note: Stretches from merely spoiled to flattened: it says ruin happened but not how much is left, where *annihilated* leaves nothing.

notes.gloss: important in effect or meaning
notes.note: More insistent than *significant*: it claims the thing matters and should be treated that way, not only that it counts.

notes.gloss: without a flaw
notes.note: Simply says there is no flaw, without the admiration that *flawless* carries.

notes.gloss: tireless
notes.note: Tireless like *unfailing*, but pictured as a pace that never slows rather than a supply that never runs out.

notes.gloss: full of life and energy
notes.note: The plain starting point: life and energy with no image attached, so every other word here colours it in some way.

notes.gloss: of low or inferior quality
notes.note: A cold comparison - it needs something better to exist before it means anything.

notes.gloss: arousing to action or rebellion
notes.note: The heat is the whole point: the thing is what lights the fire of action or rebellion, not just the occasion for it.

notes.gloss: serving or tending to provoke, excite, or stimulate; stimulating discussion or exciting controversy
notes.note: Neutral: the power to excite, stir or set off controversy, without saying if that is welcome, where *provoking* narrows it to anger.

notes.gloss: (used in combination) affected by something overwhelming
notes.note: Added to another word, its blow lands like a spell: softer-sounding than *stricken*, but just as total.

notes.gloss: lacking spontaneity or originality or individuality
notes.note: Everyday and scornful - the thing is so easy to guess that you can see it coming.

notes.gloss: a person who rescues you from harm or danger
notes.note: The grandest and most urgent of the three: it names rescue from harm or danger, not the encouragement of *uncle*.

notes.gloss: plain to see
notes.note: Mentions disguise only to deny it, suggesting that what is plain to see could have been hidden and was not.

notes.gloss: characteristic of or capable of or having a tendency toward killing another human being
notes.note: Clinical in tone and wide in reach: it covers a settled tendency to kill, the bare ability, and what is typical of killing.

notes.gloss: fail to meet the hopes or expectations of
notes.note: The mildest of the three: hopes or expectations simply fall short, without *fail*'s claim that someone was depended on and abandoned.

notes.gloss: full of spirit; full of life
notes.note: More formal than *lively* and carrying more weight: the same fullness of life, sounding like a force inside, not liveliness on show.

notes.gloss: not domesticated
notes.note: Just 'not domesticated' and nothing more - the plainest word here, with none of the menace *feral* adds.

notes.gloss: uneducated in the fundamentals of a given art or branch of learning; lacking knowledge of a specific field
notes.note: Puts the full force of 'cannot read' on one field's basics, so a limited gap sounds total - showier scorn than *ignorant*.

notes.gloss: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers
notes.note: Adds a fed-up annoyance, insisting the quality never lets up, where *utter* simply states how far it goes.

notes.gloss: causing sad feelings of gloom and inadequacy
notes.note: The flattest of these - just 'not cheerful', noting the missing cheer without the settled bleakness *cheerless* carries.

notes.gloss: an absence of emotion or enthusiasm
notes.note: The flat, general name: it covers missing emotion and missing enthusiasm alike, and treats the whole absence as a failing.

notes.gloss: destroyed completely
notes.note: Has a purpose *annihilated* lacks: somebody did it, and the word treats what was destroyed as a thing to get rid of.

notes.gloss: extremely wicked, deeply criminal
notes.note: Formal and heavy in sound: the same extreme, deeply criminal verdict as *heinous*, in grander words.

notes.gloss: not agitated; without losing self-possession
notes.note: Flatly descriptive: it notes that agitation is absent, without giving anyone credit for holding it off.

notes.gloss: difficult to accomplish; demanding considerable mental effort and skill
notes.note: Formal and weighty - it stresses the long mental effort and skill needed to get the thing done, a heavier word than *hard*.

notes.gloss: (often used ironically) worthy of being treated in a particular way
notes.note: Neutral on its face: it says some treatment is fitting, never that the treatment is good, which lets it turn ironic.

notes.gloss: capable of being reached or attained
notes.note: The same informal word written as one lump, clumsier on the page than *get-at-able* and no different in force.

notes.gloss: impossible to determine the meaning of
notes.note: Treats the thing as a code that cannot be cracked: you are beaten by the meaning, not the style as with *obscure*.

notes.gloss: gradually intrusive without right or permission
notes.note: It stresses slowness: ground taken bit by bit, so no single step looks like the violation *invasive* makes it sound.

notes.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
notes.note: Faults the thing for mileage, not damage: used so often nothing in it can still surprise, milder than the ruin *threadbare* finds.

notes.gloss: marked by excessive confidence
notes.note: The mildest word for too much confidence: an everyday word that lets the excess come across as a shrug, not an accusation.

notes.gloss: disregarded
notes.note: The mildest of the three: something was there to attend to, without *ignored*'s choice or *neglected*'s failure of care.

notes.gloss: without fault or error
notes.note: Treats being without fault as something kept whole rather than achieved, and sounds stiffer than *faultless*.

notes.gloss: an indication of damage
notes.note: The flattest word here: it records that damage happened and judges nothing, where *scar* insists the damage lasted.

notes.gloss: guilty of a misdeed
notes.note: Lighter than *criminal* because the deed is smaller: it scolds a wrong rather than condemning a crime.

notes.gloss: very unpleasant or offensive
notes.note: British slang - the unpleasantness is felt as dislike of something shabby and dirty, not the moral judgement in *filthy*.

notes.gloss: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
notes.note: Scornful, with some mockery - the person moves and acts, but the strings and the dishonesty behind it belong to whoever pulls them.

notes.gloss: an impracticable and illusory idea
notes.note: The idea is not only unreal but could never be carried out, and the word holds the picture of it bursting.

notes.gloss: of a person unable to do something skillfully
notes.note: Aimed at the person, not the result - it writes off their ability, with a fed-up feeling that can slide into fondness.

notes.gloss: the trait of acting rashly and without prudence
notes.note: Heavier, since the fault is a trait of the person, not a gap in a decision: acting without caution, not just lacking it.

notes.gloss: giving or spending with reluctance
notes.note: A softer word: *close with money* is what you say when you do not want to say *stingy*.

notes.gloss: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
notes.note: The blunt, plain-spoken version of *difficult*, taking effort of body, mind or endurance as it comes and softening none of it.

notes.gloss: entice and trap
notes.note: Enticing is only half of it - the trap closing is the other half, and that makes it land harder than *entice*.

notes.gloss: a poor example
notes.note: Regretful where *excuse* is blunt - the same judgement that it falls short, said with a pained face, not a scornful one.

notes.gloss: tending to entice into a desired action or state
notes.note: The plain name for the pull toward something wanted: it measures how strong the pull is, not where it leads, unlike *corrupting*.

notes.gloss: very clearly delineated
notes.note: Clearness of outline taken as far as it goes, next to which *sharp* sounds just good enough.

notes.gloss: lacking energy or vitality
notes.note: Clinical in tone, presenting a lack of energy as a condition to be observed rather than a failing to be judged.

notes.gloss: endowed with the capacity to reason
notes.note: Turns the simple ability to reason into a compliment, where *reasoning* and *thinking* only note that the ability is there.

notes.gloss: arousing affect
notes.note: The barest of the three — it says feeling was caused and stops there, where *poignant* and *touching* each put force behind it.

notes.gloss: acceptable to your conscience
notes.note: A low, inner bar: the thing satisfies your conscience rather than being right in itself - far weaker approval than *fitting*.

notes.gloss: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are
notes.note: The most procedural of the set: it asks only whether the steps can be carried out, not whether they should be.

notes.gloss: easily approached
notes.note: Flat and literal where *approachable* is inviting: it notes the ease and adds nothing to it.

notes.gloss: insusceptible of reform
notes.note: Makes the same refusal - it cannot be reformed - but its blunt *un-* start sounds more everyday than *irredeemable*.

notes.gloss: showing lack of skill or aptitude
notes.note: Makes the lack of skill or ability a lasting quality - not one attempt gone wrong but the person's way of doing things.

notes.gloss: made to feel uncomfortable because of shame or wounded pride
notes.note: Where *mortified* measures how sharp the discomfort is, this measures how far down it puts a person, through shame or wounded pride.

notes.gloss: devouring or craving food in great quantities
notes.note: Sounds too much like a word from a book to hurt - its strangeness softens the greed into something funny.

notes.gloss: providing or experiencing physical discomfort
notes.note: The plain general word, fitting both the thing that causes discomfort and the body that feels it, which keeps it flat.

notes.gloss: pretentiously elegant
notes.note: Scorns the elegance as put on - the height is only for show.

notes.gloss: a woman who cohabits with an important man
notes.note: Names her position without accusing her of breaking a marriage: she is defined by the home she shares and the man's standing.

notes.gloss: easily perceived and understood
notes.note: The basic, neutral word of the group: the thing takes no effort to see or understand, without *axiomatic*'s claim about proof.

notes.gloss: filled with melancholy and despondency
notes.note: Informal, with a little dry humour - it points at a turned-down mouth, not the feeling, making the state sound smaller than it is.

notes.gloss: very sophisticated especially because of surfeit; versed in the ways of the world
notes.note: Sophistication from having had too much, which sours the praise: the person is past being impressed, where *worldly* only means experienced.

notes.gloss: uncomfortable because of possible danger or trouble
notes.note: Places the discomfort in possible danger or trouble, not in the body, and its mildness is what makes it sound like a warning.

notes.gloss: lacking seriousness; given to frivolity
notes.note: Mockery that goes past unserious to empty: nothing inside to be serious with, where *dizzy* only sets the head spinning.

notes.gloss: foolish or senseless behavior
notes.note: Heavy and sternly critical - it treats the behaviour as a failure of judgement serious enough to name, where *craziness* simply calls it mad.

notes.gloss: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
notes.note: The same promise as *arable*, seen through the act of cultivating: an open possibility, not a fixed label for the land.

notes.gloss: having odor or a characteristic odor
notes.note: The base word: having a smell, or a smell of its own, and the only one here that never says which smell.

notes.gloss: exhibiting native good judgment
notes.note: The heaviest of the *commonsense* forms: its extra ending makes the same praise sound clumsier than crisp *commonsense* itself.

notes.gloss: an ugly evil-looking old woman
notes.note: Disgust and nothing more: the same ugly, evil-looking figure as *witch* but without power, so it mocks where *witch* shrinks back.

notes.gloss: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
notes.note: Keeps the secrecy in view - what is told was meant to be kept, so the telling counts as a breach.

notes.gloss: damaged by blows or hard usage
notes.note: Informal where *battered* is not, treating the same hard usage as something to shrug at rather than record.

notes.gloss: mentally or physically infirm with age
notes.note: The same judgement of weakness from age as *doddering*, but the shorter form makes the mockery sound casual rather than deliberate.

notes.gloss: the quality of being worthy of esteem or respect
notes.note: Highest and steadiest here: not a feeling about oneself but a worth that earns respect, so never open to *conceit*'s charge of excess.

notes.gloss: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated or cultivated
notes.note: The same natural state as *wild*, but described by what was never done to it: a taming that never happened.

notes.gloss: showing a sense of guilt
notes.note: Scornful, and it paints a picture: guilt shown as a shrinking, beaten posture, and the word enjoys saying so.

notes.gloss: (used especially of persons) having lived for a relatively long time or attained a specific age
notes.note: Flat and neutral, it covers both a long life lived and simply a stated age reached, where *of age* means only the second.

notes.gloss: something many people believe that is false
notes.note: The gentlest way to call a common belief false: a passing idea, not an accusation against those who hold it.

notes.gloss: exceedingly; extremely
notes.note: The adverb of *fabulous*: extravagant - praise pitched at the ceiling and past plausibility, far louder than *pleasing*.

notes.gloss: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
notes.note: Reaches from scorched to gone: it names fire as the cause but leaves open how much survives, where *burned-out* pins that down.

notes.gloss: having or showing great excitement and interest
notes.note: The plain word: it reports the excitement and interest without judging whether they are deserved, the very thing *overenthusiastic* judges.

notes.gloss: peculiarly fortunate or appropriate; as if by divine intervention
notes.note: Deeply thankful - the timing was so right it tempts you to say heaven stepped in.

notes.gloss: readily apparent to the mind
notes.note: The plain word: a thing reaches the mind without effort, and it does not say whether that is a good thing.

notes.gloss: the act of hindering or obstructing or impeding
notes.note: The broadest of the three, covering holding back, blocking and slowing alike, and picturing the act as a course disrupted from outside.

notes.gloss: inspired by love for your country
notes.note: The same love of country, but as faithful attachment rather than passion - quieter and less openly shown than *patriotic*.

notes.gloss: implied though not directly expressed; inherent in the nature of something
notes.note: Built as 'not explicit', it sees the telling as falling short, where *implicit* sees a quality of the thing itself.

notes.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
notes.note: The easiest word here to hear without complaint: anything beyond what is needed can simply be available, where *superfluous* would call it waste.

notes.gloss: verging on the indecent
notes.note: The lightest criticism here - close to indecent but not quite there, so it scolds where *obscene* accuses.

notes.gloss: aroused to impatience or anger
notes.note: Churning, not flaring: the feeling is muddy and unsettled all through, where *stung* is one sharp point.

notes.gloss: causing mental or emotional injury
notes.note: Borrows the body's word for hurt to mind or feelings: the damage is a blow that leaves a mark, not *harmful*'s bare capacity.

notes.gloss: containing errors or alterations
notes.note: Points back to a sound original that errors or changes have since got into, where *corrupt* just describes how it is now.

notes.gloss: being precisely fitting and right
notes.note: The same verdict as *fitting*, declared in a serious, formal way, so the rightness sounds handed down rather than noticed.

notes.gloss: arising from or marked by despair or loss of hope
notes.note: Points at the despair itself, whether a thing comes from lost hope or just shows it, where *hopeless* points at the chances.

notes.gloss: greatly annoyed; out of patience
notes.note: British, and it takes the drama out: patience fully lost, in a phrase too casual to shout, where *exasperated* keeps its calm.

notes.gloss: act as an informer
notes.note: Makes the act a role: you are not someone who spoke but an informer, and the role carries a faint stain *tell* lacks.

notes.gloss: belligerence aroused by a real or supposed wrong (personified as one of the deadly sins)
notes.note: The plain name for hostility at a wrong that may be real or only supposed, so the blame lands lighter than in *wrath*.

notes.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
notes.note: Puts the wear down to time, not to any user - unlike *hackneyed*, which blames someone for running the thing into the ground.

notes.gloss: having or covered with or accompanied by blood
notes.note: The plain word for blood in a thing, on it, or simply alongside it, and it judges none of these.

notes.gloss: inspiring admiration or approval
notes.note: Approval with respect in it - you look up to the thing rather than just enjoy it, a more serious word than *charming*.

notes.gloss: in a more fortunate or prosperous condition
notes.note: Built as a comparison - it always means better than something, and never says what.

notes.gloss: absorbed in your own interests or thoughts etc
notes.note: The same fault as *self-absorbed*, easy to forgive, and the milder way to say it.

notes.gloss: foolish; totally unsound
notes.note: Joking - the foolishness is treated as amusing oddness, so it stings less than *crazy*, though the verdict is the same.

notes.gloss: expressing yourself readily, clearly, effectively
notes.note: Approves of how the words come out - without friction - and is a plainer word than *eloquent*.

notes.gloss: given or inflicted in requital according to merits or deserts
notes.note: Cool and measured: it approves the match between what is deserved and what is dealt out, not what is dealt out itself.

notes.gloss: thrown into a state of disorganization or incoherence
notes.note: Pictures the collapse as a coming-apart: what was holding gives way, and the thing falls into disorder or stops making sense.

notes.gloss: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
notes.note: Puts the outcome in the person's own mind, so it holds even if nothing is done, unlike *target*, something that can be hit.

notes.gloss: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
notes.note: Approval at its lowest: it grants only that the manner was not rude, where *polite* can stretch to social rules kept well enough.

notes.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
notes.note: Formal, and it marks the statement as the kind that makes someone look small, where *denigrating* catches the act as it happens.

notes.gloss: not made explicit
notes.note: Sounds clinical: the gap is a failure to put something into words, not a silence with any weight to it.

notes.gloss: not functioning properly
notes.note: The gentlest word here — it notes that something is off without saying how far or how badly.

notes.gloss: with sincerity; without pretense
notes.note: The adverb of *unfeigned*: defined against pretence, which is a curious way to have to say it.

notes.gloss: affected by blight; anything that mars or prevents growth or prosperity
notes.note: British spelling, and milder: the good has gone out of it, where *blighted* adds that nothing will come of it now.

notes.gloss: causing dejection
notes.note: Lowers the spirits in a small, stale way: too minor for the wide reach of *dismal*, but enough to bring a mood down.

notes.gloss: reflecting optimism
notes.note: Puts the optimism in what is shown, not in whoever holds it - it colours a view instead of judging a person's nature.

notes.gloss: most unfortunate or miserable
notes.note: Holds nothing back - misfortune or misery as bad as it gets, where *unfortunate* only notes that luck ran out.

notes.gloss: firm in purpose or belief; characterized by firmness and determination
notes.note: Formal and settled, covering belief as well as purpose: firmness as a lasting quality of the person, not a stand taken once.

notes.gloss: not caused to be equal
notes.note: Points at what was not done - nothing has been made equal - where *unequal* judges the gap that remains.

notes.gloss: murder without leaving a trace on the body
notes.note: Chilling because so exact: it names the killing by its method, no trace left on the body, where *murder* is general.

notes.gloss: the state of being held in high esteem and honor
notes.note: The same high respect and honor as *reputation*, said in a more formal way.

notes.gloss: causing dejection
notes.note: Gloom from dull sameness: it makes a mood flat rather than dark, lowering the spirits without the threat of *grim*.

notes.gloss: characterized by thriftiness
notes.note: The flat word: it names care with resources as a lasting trait, without pressing the approval *thrifty* carries.

notes.gloss: difficult to understand
notes.note: Has exactly the force of *incomprehensible* but sounds put together on the spot, its un- plainer than the in-.

notes.gloss: responsible for or chargeable with a reprehensible act
notes.note: The plain verdict, covering both the one who did the wrong and the one who could merely be charged with it.

notes.gloss: marked by sound judgment; having good reason
notes.note: Sound judgment as the basic standard a mind must meet, not a prize it wins, which gives it a weight *reasonable* lacks.

notes.gloss: free of extraneous elements of any kind
notes.note: The broadest word here: nothing that does not belong, of any kind, survives it, where *clean* only rules out dirt.

notes.gloss: aroused to impatience or anger
notes.note: Light: it treats the feeling as a small thing and the person as easily upset, where *annoyed* judges neither.

notes.gloss: a partiality for some particular place
notes.note: Names the leaning by its object, one particular place, so the narrow view is built in, where *partiality* must spell it out.

notes.gloss: free from flaw or blemish or impurity
notes.note: Goes beyond flaws and marks to anything mixed in that spoils it, so it can describe a substance, not only a performance.

notes.gloss: snarled or stalled in complete confusion
notes.note: The same total tangle or standstill under a short, almost casual label - a sad smile where *fucked-up* is furious.

notes.gloss: an indication of damage
notes.note: Damage dragged across a surface — broader than *scratch* and still shallow.

notes.gloss: put trust in with confidence
notes.note: Settled, nothing held back: the trust is already placed and resting there, with none of the risk still heard in *bet*.

notes.gloss: (of persons) worthy of trust or confidence
notes.note: The *-ed* form makes the trust something others give, where *sure* names a quality the person carries on their own.

notes.gloss: causing dejection
notes.note: The plain middle of the family: it names the low spirits it causes without making them stronger, where *dismal* passes judgement.

notes.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
notes.note: Names the laugh the thing draws, dismissing it with amusement where *preposterous* rejects it out loud.

notes.gloss: barely credible
notes.note: Leaves the thing only just believable, where *incredible* puts it past belief, and the stretch sounds like extravagance, not a fault.

notes.gloss: excessively or unduly careful
notes.note: Blunter than *overcareful*: 'too' spells out the excess in plain words, where *overcareful* tucks it into the front of the word.

notes.gloss: affecting or influenced by the human mind
notes.note: Works both ways, covering what the mind affects and what affects it, where *psychogenic* looks only at where a thing began.

notes.gloss: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
notes.note: Only says something was made bigger; the fault is in going too far, not the word, so it accuses least of the three.

notes.gloss: cheerfully irresponsible
notes.note: Showy boldness rather than lightness - it shows off not caring, where *carefree* simply has no worry to shed.

notes.gloss: showing lack of art
notes.note: Names something missing, not a mess - the work shows no art, a lighter complaint than the spoiling *botched* points at.

notes.gloss: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
notes.note: Treats the matter as buried, not just untold, so digging is part of the word - unlike *reveal*.

notes.gloss: lure by imitating the characteristic call of an animal
notes.note: Neutral and technical: the lure is an imitated animal cry, so all the trickery is in the sound, none in any promise.

notes.gloss: not subdued or trained for service or use
notes.note: Neither brought under control nor trained for service or use - its wildness is measured by what it has not been made to do.

notes.gloss: an impudent or insolent rejoinder
notes.note: Bluntly scolding - the disrespectful answer reduced to just talk, named by the body part that made it, not by what it said.

notes.gloss: not pleased; experiencing or manifesting displeasure
notes.note: The coolest word here: it names a lack of pleasure, felt or shown, without any heat in it.

notes.gloss: physically or spiritually homeless or deprived of security
notes.note: The plain word, for someone without a roof or without inner security, with none of the sense of being wronged in *dispossessed*.

notes.gloss: filled or scattered with a disorderly accumulation of objects or rubbish
notes.note: About too many things rather than dirt; a cluttered desk can still be working.

notes.gloss: containing errors or alterations
notes.note: Errors or changes have got in, so it can't be trusted as it is - heavier than *flawed*, where the whole stays sound.

notes.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
notes.note: Formal and angry, rejecting the absurdity out loud rather than just laughing at it as *laughable* does.

notes.gloss: call upon in supplication; entreat
notes.note: Pleading at its most formal - an appeal made from a humble stance rather than *beg*'s bare asking.

notes.gloss: showing intellectual penetration or emotional depth
notes.note: The strongest and widest here, praising a mind that cuts through or a feeling that runs deep, where *deep* stays with thinking.

notes.gloss: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
notes.note: Heavier and fuller-sounding than *platitudinal*, and the word's own size is part of the mockery: dullness dressed up, then shown up.

notes.gloss: imparting vitality and energy
notes.note: Cool, calm approval: it steadies you and gives you energy, but does not delight you like the louder *exhilarating*.

notes.gloss: overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors
notes.note: A flat accusation: the swollen self-esteem of *pride* turned outward, as an overbearing, superior manner toward those it looks down on.

notes.gloss: not appropriate in application; defective
notes.note: Formal and softened: it calls a thing unsuited to its use and faulty, while sounding sorry about it, where *inept* simply condemns.

notes.gloss: thrown into a state of disarray or confusion
notes.note: Names the lost order as a state the thing has been put into and left in, without the damage *broken* implies.

notes.gloss: decisively surpassed by something else so as to appear to be of a lower class
notes.note: The strongest here: the low standing comes from a contest clearly lost, and carries the humiliation of the comparison.

notes.gloss: in the nature of something though not readily apparent
notes.note: A linking phrase, not a quality: it must name what the meaning lies in, which *inherent* and *underlying* need not.

notes.gloss: spoiled and covered with eggs and larvae of flies
notes.note: The same eggs and larvae as *flyblown*, but with the crawling maggots right in front of you - the harder word to hear.

notes.gloss: not noticed
notes.note: The flat, basic word: it says only that the thing was not noticed, blaming no one and giving it no claim on attention.

notes.gloss: expecting a rise in prices
notes.note: A stance, not a judgement: it names an expectation of rising prices, and unlike *optimistic* says nothing about the person holding it.

notes.gloss: precisely as stated
notes.note: Plain emphasis, insisting the thing is exactly the one stated and carrying no praise or blame with it.

notes.gloss: not derivative or imitative
notes.note: Praises a thing by what it is not - not taken from a source, not a copy - and, unlike *original*, claims no freshness.

notes.gloss: completely unordered and unpredictable and confusing
notes.note: Blames the state for confusing anyone following it: no order, nothing predictable, where *wild* only says control is gone.

notes.gloss: unable to function; without help
notes.note: Unable to function and without help, like *helpless*, but as a settled state rather than a moment, so it sounds beyond rescue.

notes.gloss: not serious in content or attitude or behavior
notes.note: The plain word here and the widest, fitting content, attitude or behaviour alike, without the hollow-head picture of *airheaded* or *empty-headed*.

notes.gloss: something jumbled or confused
notes.note: Makes the mess or confusion something you are inside and lost in, complicated in a way *tangle* does not suggest.

notes.gloss: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
notes.note: Notes the trait as a sign the thing carries, crediting it lightly where *distinguish* lifts it.

notes.gloss: irritable as if suffering from indigestion
notes.note: Very old-fashioned and fancy - bad temper dressed up as a physical illness, and hard to say with a straight face.

notes.gloss: reduced to nothingness
notes.note: The bare form, without *-ed*, says flatly that nothing is left, with no look back at what caused it, which *obliterated* keeps.

notes.gloss: poorly done
notes.note: Dismissive, with a touch of scorn - the badness is rough and uneven, plain to see in the thing itself.

notes.gloss: have faith or confidence in
notes.note: Treats the faith as a stake laid down, admitting in the same breath that it could be lost, which *rely* never does.

notes.gloss: the mental ability to understand and discriminate between relations
notes.note: The flat name for the ability to tell relations apart, saying only that it is there, without the admiration *sagacity* adds.

notes.gloss: able to make or detect effects of great subtlety; sensitive
notes.note: Praises a perception fine enough to make and catch effects too subtle for a duller eye, where *selective* only picks among the obvious.

notes.gloss: reveal unintentionally
notes.note: The teller never meant to tell: it slips out and gives them away, so the fault is the slip, not the intent.

notes.gloss: nonexistent
notes.note: Treats the absence as a shortfall rather than a plain fact, which is how *absent* states it.

notes.gloss: having or showing or indicative of high or elevated character
notes.note: The basic word here for the thing itself: having high character, showing it, or merely pointing to it.

notes.gloss: a female person who is a fellow member of a sorority or labor union or other group
notes.note: Turns fellow membership of a union, a sorority or any other group into a family tie between women, warmer than plain *member*.

notes.gloss: morally binding or necessary
notes.note: Formal and serious: it ties the duty to whoever it rests on, where *mandatory* states it as a general rule.

notes.gloss: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
notes.note: Hints rather than accuses: the evil lies behind what is seen, in a thing's source as much as in the thing itself.

notes.gloss: (used of decomposing oils or fats) having a rank smell or taste usually due to a chemical change or decomposition
notes.note: Names the strong, foul smell or taste of decaying fats and oils - an accusation from the senses, not *bad*'s bare ruling.

notes.gloss: unerringly accurate
notes.note: Informal and total: accuracy with no room for error at all, where *precise* can still be more or less exact.

notes.gloss: causing fear or dread or terror
notes.note: The *-ed* form turns it around: the thing is defined by the dread already aimed at it, where *dreadful* says it causes dread.

notes.gloss: the humane quality of understanding the suffering of others and wanting to do something about it
notes.note: Praise in this sense, a kind quality, but the word tilts down toward the sufferer where *compassion* stands level.

notes.gloss: more familiar or renowned than the other of two
notes.note: Narrow - it compares exactly two and gives one the edge, not the top spot among all as *best-known* does.

notes.gloss: extended meanings; especially of psychological coldness; without human warmth or emotion
notes.note: The plain word: it names missing human warmth without deciding whether that is a settled nature or a snub aimed at someone.

notes.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
notes.note: An accounting word: it records the amount left over as a balance, with no complaint about it.

notes.gloss: an instance that does not conform to a rule or generalization
notes.note: Names a case by where it stands - outside the rule - and passes no judgement on it for being there.

notes.gloss: showing inappropriate levity
notes.note: The verdict is built in, since the lightness is out of place: it scolds a manner, where *empty-headed* diagnoses a mind.

notes.gloss: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
notes.note: Sees the same pretending to impress as an act put on for an audience, with more scorn for the performance than *appearance* has.

notes.gloss: without hope because there seems to be no possibility of comfort or success
notes.note: The plain verdict: no hope because no comfort or success looks possible - about the odds, where *despairing* is about the feeling.

notes.gloss: causing or tending to cause anger or resentment
notes.note: The *-ing* form keeps the effect happening: anger or resentment being stirred now, where *agitative* names a settled quality.

notes.gloss: not current or belonging to the present time
notes.note: The flattest word here - it simply says something does not belong to the present, without the judgement *obsolete* passes.

notes.gloss: improper or even offensive
notes.note: Sounds mild but runs from merely improper to offensive, and saying it so mildly gives the offensive end its force.

notes.gloss: based on interpretation; not directly expressed
notes.note: Carries no approval - it says how something is reached, by interpretation, not statement, where *constructive* judges the worth of what is done.

notes.gloss: destroyed financially
notes.note: Financial ruin in the bluntest word: a single snap rather than a decline, with no blame on the one it fell on.

notes.gloss: highly attractive and able to arouse hope or desire
notes.note: The attraction works like a spell that holds you, so the hope it raises feels made by magic, where *alluring* simply glows.

notes.gloss: tending to impart new life and vigor to
notes.note: Approval for a lift that brings back lost life and energy, rather than giving them for the first time like *life-giving*.

notes.gloss: feeling shame or guilt or embarrassment or remorse
notes.note: The plain word for the feeling, wide enough for guilt and remorse as well as shame; unlike *disgraced*, it says nothing about reputation.

notes.gloss: belligerence aroused by a real or supposed wrong (personified as one of the deadly sins)
notes.note: The same hostility raised to solemn weight: a word sized for a sin, where *anger* is sized for a mood.

notes.gloss: the goal intended to be attained (and which is believed to be attainable)
notes.note: Dry and formal: the goal as a definite thing to get, one believed within reach, without *target*'s sense of hit or miss.

notes.gloss: humble in spirit or manner; suggesting retiring mildness or even cowed submissiveness
notes.note: Approves of a quiet, held-back manner - mildness as a virtue, though the meaning can come close to giving in to others.

notes.gloss: mentally or physically infirm with age
notes.note: Scornful where *aged* is not: weakness of mind or body from age becomes the whole of what it says about the person.

notes.gloss: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules
notes.note: Plain approval no one can argue with: it confirms nobody was favored or tricked, without the weight of principle *just* carries.

notes.gloss: the ultimate goal for which something is done
notes.note: Makes the outcome the final one that everything else serves, and brings the picture of a journey's end that *object* lacks.

notes.gloss: (often followed by ‘from’) not alike; different in nature or quality
notes.note: Makes the difference a matter of telling things apart, so it holds up to a close look, where *distinct* just states it.

notes.gloss: free of restrictions or qualifications
notes.note: The same freedom as *clean*, but as an open way through: nothing in the way, rather than nothing left over.

notes.gloss: without ceremony or formality
notes.note: Pictures the ceremony or formality as stripped off, with an abrupt, blunt edge that *casual* never carries.

notes.gloss: serenely self-possessed and free from agitation especially in times of stress
notes.note: Approving of calm kept up on purpose while the pressure is on, not the luck of an easy hour.

notes.gloss: resembling swine; coarsely gluttonous or greedy
notes.note: The *-y* ending makes the pig little - small enough to carry no real anger.

notes.gloss: (of an alcoholic drink) stirred or shaken with ice, but served without it
notes.note: A serving instruction, not a judgement: the drink was stirred or shaken with ice, then served without it.

notes.gloss: advanced in years; (‘aged’ is pronounced as two syllables)
notes.note: Formal and weighty, it presents advanced years as a settled state, where *older* only marks a point on a scale.

notes.gloss: not noticed inadvertently
notes.note: The same accidental slip as *disregarded*, but implying the thing once held attention and lost it, leaving it a little less important.

notes.gloss: constant and unchanging
notes.note: Absolute and cool: it states that a thing does not change, without the praise for holding firm that *steadfast* carries.

notes.gloss: a term of address for an elderly woman
notes.note: Said to an old woman rather than about her, and calling her this gives her the standing of family.

notes.gloss: having a strong distaste from surfeit
notes.note: Strong dislike from having had too much of something - the stomach turning, not anger aimed at anyone.

notes.gloss: properly or sufficiently qualified or capable or efficient
notes.note: The mildest approval here: it sets a minimum and says it was met - qualified, capable or efficient enough, and no more.

notes.gloss: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
notes.note: Ruin on the scale of *disaster*, but declared in a grander, more ringing way.

notes.gloss: a disposition to exhibit uncontrolled anger
notes.note: Not a passing mood but a settled tendency to anger that gets out of hand - an accusation about someone's character.

notes.gloss: the trait of remaining calm and seeming not to care; a casual lack of concern
notes.note: Stresses the calm, casual side - an untroubled evenness that may only be on the surface, without *indifference*'s hint that nothing is felt.

notes.gloss: lacking freshness, palatability, or showing deterioration from age
notes.note: The plainest word for lost freshness - taste gone, or condition gone with age - where *bad* goes further: unfit to eat.

notes.gloss: not having or showing or requiring special skill or proficiency
notes.note: Labels rather than condemns - it fits work needing no special skill as evenly as a worker without it, where *botchy* judges the result.

notes.gloss: make illegal payments to in exchange for favors or influence
notes.note: The plain word for buying, turned on a person, hints scornfully that they had a price, where *bribe* names the crime.

notes.gloss: done by hand without mechanical aids or devices
notes.note: Purely about method - the hand working without mechanical aid or device - with none of the approval the words beside it carry.

notes.gloss: covered with or smelling of mold
notes.note: The gentlest of the three words for mold seen on the food or smelled off it, with none of *moldy*'s bluntness.

notes.gloss: lacking energy or vitality
notes.note: Technical, not judging: the lack of energy sounds like a lasting feature, not the passing drain that *enervated* suggests.
